title: Civil status and spouse for the pension fund
purpose: Ask the civil status once. Map it to the pension fund's list and to the source tax view, and ask the spouse's or registered partner's date of birth when the fund registers the employee as Married.

stories.title: Ask the civil status once, using the pension fund's list
stories.i_want: to state my civil status once, choosing from Single, Married, Divorced, Widowed, Registered partnership and Separated
stories.so_that: the pension fund registration and the source tax tariff can both use my answer without asking me again
stories.priority_reason: Civil status is a required field of the pension fund registration; a registration without it is rejected. Source tax also needs it to set the tariff letter.

acceptance_criteria.title: Civil status is always asked and required
acceptance_criteria.given: any new employee filling in the questionnaire, in the 'Civil status and spouse' step
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee reaches the civil status question
acceptance_criteria.then: the civil status is asked of every employee, whatever their country of residence, nationality or source tax situation, and the questionnaire cannot be submitted without an answer

acceptance_criteria.title: Allowed values
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee answers the civil status question
acceptance_criteria.then: they can choose exactly one of: Single, Married, Divorced, Widowed, Registered partnership, Separated. The first four are the pension fund's own list; Registered partnership and Separated are added because the source tax calculator distinguishes them and the fund's list has no option for them (see OQ-civil-status-partnership)

acceptance_criteria.title: Asked once, reused for every receiving party
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has answered the civil status
acceptance_criteria.when: the pension fund and source tax need the civil status
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is not asked again in any later step (including the source tax step); the answer is recorded for the pension fund, translated to the fund's list, and for source tax, grouped as married/registered partnership or not married

stories.title: Ask the spouse's or partner's date of birth from married, partnered and separated employees
stories.i_want: the date of birth of the husband, wife or registered partner of every employee I register as Married
stories.so_that: the registration is complete and not rejected with 'Spouse's date of birth is required'
stories.priority_reason: The fund rejects a Married registration without the spouse's date of birth, which blocks the registration.

acceptance_criteria.title: Asked and required for Married, Registered partnership and Separated
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has answered the civil status
acceptance_criteria.when: the civil status is Married, Registered partnership or Separated (all entered at the fund as Married)
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is asked the date of birth of their spouse or registered partner (for separated employees: of the spouse they are still married to), and cannot submit without it. The date is recorded for the pension fund

acceptance_criteria.title: Not asked for Single, Divorced or Widowed
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has answered the civil status
acceptance_criteria.when: the civil status is Single, Divorced or Widowed
acceptance_criteria.then: no spouse or partner date of birth is asked (data minimisation). Whether the fund needs further fields for Divorced or Widowed is not known (see OQ-spouse-dob-other-status)

acceptance_criteria.title: Date form
acceptance_criteria.given: the spouse's or partner's date of birth is asked
acceptance_criteria.then: it is a full date given as DD.MM.YYYY, as the pension fund expects it

acceptance_criteria.title: Discarded when the civil status changes before submission
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee entered a spouse's date of birth and then changes the civil status to Single, Divorced or Widowed
acceptance_criteria.then: the spouse's date of birth is not kept; if the employee switches back before submitting, the earlier input may still be there

stories.title: Enter the civil status in the pension fund's terms
stories.i_want: every employee's civil status expressed in my list (Single, Married, Divorced, Widowed)
stories.so_that: the registration can be made with a valid civil status, even for registered partners and separated employees
stories.priority_reason: Civil status is a required fund field; a value outside the fund's list would block the registration.

acceptance_criteria.title: Fund's own values taken as answered
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee's civil status is Single, Married, Divorced or Widowed
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio records the civil status for the pension fund
acceptance_criteria.then: the same value is recorded for the fund

acceptance_criteria.title: Registered partnership and Separated entered as Married (provisional)
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee's civil status is Registered partnership or Separated, which the fund's list does not contain
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio records the civil status for the pension fund
acceptance_criteria.then: Married is recorded for the fund, together with the partner's or spouse's date of birth. This mapping is provisional until a domain expert and the fund confirm it (see OQ-civil-status-partnership)

acceptance_criteria.title: Always derived from the latest civil status
acceptance_criteria.given: the civil status recorded for the fund is derived from the employee's answer
acceptance_criteria.when: the civil status answer changes (before submission by the employee, afterwards by HR)
acceptance_criteria.then: the civil status for the fund is derived again from the latest answer; the employee is never asked for it separately

stories.title: Group the civil status for source tax
stories.i_want: the employee's civil status grouped as the calculator does: married or registered partnership, or not married (single, divorced, separated, widowed)
stories.so_that: the right spouse questions, spouse exemption and tariff letter apply without asking the civil status again
stories.priority_reason: The grouping decides the tariff letter (A/B/C/H) and the spouse exemption; a wrong group gives a wrong tariff code.

acceptance_criteria.title: Married and Registered partnership count as married
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee's civil status is Married or Registered partnership
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio derives the civil status for source tax
acceptance_criteria.then: it is 'Married or registered partnership', including for the spouse exemption

acceptance_criteria.title: Single, Divorced, Widowed and Separated count as not married
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee's civil status is Single, Divorced, Widowed or Separated
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio derives the civil status for source tax
acceptance_criteria.then: it is 'Not married'; in particular a separated employee counts as not married for source tax, although the fund registers them as Married

acceptance_criteria.title: Derived, not asked again
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has answered the civil status
acceptance_criteria.when: the source tax step needs the calculator's civil status
acceptance_criteria.then: the grouping is derived from the latest civil status answer and the employee is not asked the calculator's civil status question
